correctness.rationale: The 2-round EF game and the four quadrant masks give an exact all-permutation first-order rank-two invariant. The correct sum/skew transitions act by adding right-above and left-below, or right-below and left-above, to every child mask respectively. The actual certificate lists 226 distinct reachable states, explicit valid separable witnesses and a minimum-cost binary derivation for each. Checking all 226 squared ordered pairs for both operations proves full closure; checking universal minimum-length subadditivity and attained witness sizes proves exact minima for every all-size derivation. Independent direct enumeration of all separable permutations through ten agrees. The excluded nonseparable example has signature 37928, absent from the exhaustive closure. Finite experiments support the proof but are not alone offered as an all-size argument.

value.rationale: Separable permutations form a canonical recursively generated class (equivalent to cograph permutation graphs), and rank two is the first useful two-round observational horizon for their two-order representations. The exact 226-class quotient and sharp ten-point representative bound describe a natural finite-model-theoretic invariant and give a provably complete minimal test-size cutoff. The five-point external signature reveals a genuine logical boundary of the class. The number 226 cannot be read off from Schröder counts, is not an arbitrary parameter slice, and the all-size finite-state certificate is essential to the result.
